newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova links Russian pullout to Dnestr accord.
newsitem.headline: Moldova links Russian pullout to Dnestr accord.

text.p: Moldova has agreed to link the withdrawal of Russian troops from its Dnestr region with a political settlement for the breakaway territory, President Petru Lucinschi said on Wednesday.

"Russian troops will be reduced to 2,500 irrespective of any settlement but a complete pullout must be linked to the final political settlement of the Dnestr conflict," Lucinschi told a news conference.

He was speaking a day after meeting President Boris Yeltsin in the Kremlin, on his first visit to Moscow since being elected president of the tiny ex-Soviet republic last December on a platform of closer ties with Russia.
Russian troops played a crucial role in ending bloody clashes between Moldovan forces and Dnestr separatists in 1992. Some 6,000 troops remain in Moldova as a peace-keeping force.

Lucinschi said a complete withdrawal without a peace accord would create a security vacuum. "The Moldovan national army would directly face the Dnestr army, which is almost as strong as ours," he added.
Moldova says it is ready to grant broad autonomy to the Dnestr region, a sliver of industrial land that borders Ukraine, but separatist leaders insist on full independence.
Lucinschi said Yeltsin had agreed to help set up a permanent group of experts that would elaborate a draft law on the Dnestr region's special status within the Moldovan republic.
He said he thought the Moldovan parliament could adopt such a law by the end of this year.

Lucinschi said planned visits to Moldova in the near future by Ukrainan President Leonid Kuchma and Russia's Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov would help speed up a settlement in the Dnestr region and establish a timetable for withdrawing Russian troops.
Moldova and Russia signed an agreement in 1994 to withdraw Moscow's troops within three years, but it was never ratified by the Russian State Duma lower house of the parliament.
